clue.text: Going to the front, place of duty for nurse

definitions.meaning: moving forwards, advancing
a nurse on duty is stationed on a hospital ward

explanation.surface: A nurse heads to the front line to serve in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancing forwards is going this way, and a nurse working is posted on a hospital ward.

clue.text: A well-armed denizen of the deep

definitions.text: A well-armed denizen of the deep

parts.words: A well-armed denizen of the deep
parts.note: well-armed means having many arms, eight of them, not weapons

explanation.surface: A heavily armed sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-armed' means having lots of limbs, eight in this case.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-limbed sea creature lives in the ocean.

clue.text: Exhausted, having had a session in the gym

definitions.meaning: used up, depleted, as a mine may be

definitions.text: having had a session in the gym
definitions.meaning: having exercised

explanation.surface: Tired after a gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: A depleted mine is used up; someone who has exercised has trained.

clue.text: Fire at it and you'll probably miss

definitions.text: Fire at it and you'll probably miss

parts.words: Fire at it and you'll probably miss

explanation.surface: A warning about a hard target.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'fire at' plus the answer means to shoot without aiming.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting without aim, haphazardly, is likely to miss.

clue.text: Oh boy! All round publicity!

indicators.note: turning the letters round signals that these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excited cry about publicity reaching everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as 'all round', meaning everywhere, but it is the anagram signal working on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy promotional fuss is a lively word for publicity.

clue.text: A strange kind of lily

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd variety of lily.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant family of lily-like flowers.

clue.text: Much less neglect

definitions.meaning: used as in 'I can't walk, much less run'
to leave something alone

explanation.surface: Far less ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'still less' in a sentence, and also to leave something untouched.

clue.text: Stout novelist and comedian

definitions.meaning: sturdy and tough
Thomas, who wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles, and Oliver, partner of Stan Laurel, share this surname

explanation.surface: A portly novelist who was also a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means tough, and Thomas the writer and Oliver the comedian share the name.

clue.text: Regular soldier?

definitions.meaning: neat and well arranged
a soldier who attends an officer, or a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A soldier in the regular army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular soldier' looks like one phrase, but it is two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and methodical is one sense; a soldier serving as an officer's attendant is the other.

clue.text: Man in the seat of power

indicators.note: one piece placed in another, so the name goes inside the word given by 'the'

explanation.surface: A man sits in the seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a link word in the surface, but it is the container signal; a common man's name sits inside the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair stands for royal power itself.

clue.text: Pearl may be sophisticated

definitions.meaning: a pearl grown on an oyster farm is a ... pearl
refined and educated

explanation.surface: A pearl can be classy.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmed pearl has this name, and a refined, well-read person is described the same way.

clue.text: You may take work home from it

definitions.text: You may take work home from it

parts.words: You may take work home from it
parts.note: work here is a book borrowed, not a job brought home from the office

explanation.surface: A place one brings work home from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' suggests a job, but a work is a book you borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are lent from this building to take home.

clue.text: Capital turn of a pierrot

indicators.note: a turn here is a change, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clown gives a splendid performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of' looks like a clown's act, but it signals rearranging A PIERROT. A pierrot is a sad clown in a white costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital city of South Africa.

clue.text: Not necessarily the golfer

parts.note: Gary is a famous South African golfer with this surname, but anyone taking part in a game shares the word

explanation.surface: A participant, though not specifically the famous golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Player is a famous golfer; the clue says any participant in a game has the name too.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes part in a sport or game is a participant, of which the golfer is one example.

clue.text: I'm badly upset by such an impulse

indicators.note: upset badly means the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone made upset by a sudden urge.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving force or stimulus behind an action.

clue.text: Gunned down in an attempt

definitions.meaning: fired at and hit with a gun
a go or try at something

explanation.surface: Someone shot in a failed bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit by a bullet is one sense; a try or go at something is another.

clue.text: Head ball on to right winger

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance or ball
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A footballer heads the ball on to the right winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides the politics: 'right winger' is TORY, a British Conservative; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is called a head, as in Beachy Head.

clue.text: Fail to turn out as intended

definitions.text: Fail to turn out as intended

parts.words: Fail to turn out as intended
parts.note: turn out here means get out of bed in time

explanation.surface: A plan that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' means rise from bed, not result.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping past the time one meant to wake up.

clue.text: One's fiance proposed

definitions.meaning: a person's future spouse
planned or meant

explanation.surface: A fiance who was proposed to.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed partner is one's future spouse; a planned thing is meant.

clue.text: Arrange to send away for goods

definitions.meaning: to sort into a proper sequence
read as 'put in an order', to place an order for goods

explanation.surface: Setting up a mail order for products.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is one sense; placing a request with a supplier for goods is the other.

clue.text: A plain repair I made a mess of

indicators.note: messing up these letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Botching a repair to flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide grassland plain, as in North America.

clue.text: The lady's ring is one much admired

parts.note: her is the possessive form for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's ring belongs to someone she admires.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolised person is admired for brave or great deeds.

clue.text: Available to discuss outside

parts.note: to air a topic is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Free to talk outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors, not under a roof.

clue.text: Do well to take the short cut

annotationWithheld.why: Do well to take the short cut (6): THRIVE is defined by 'Do well', but no parse of 'take the short cut' gives THRIVE (or its remaining letters); search found no source for the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Do well to take the short cut

clue.text: Old soldier taking flight

parts.note: a fighter of old whose arrows fly, not a deserter running off

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking flight' suggests fleeing, but it is the arrows that fly from a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman in an old army shot arrows through the air.

clue.text: Fresh scrip issue

indicators.note: an issue sends the letters out again, rearranged

explanation.surface: A new share issue.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrip is a share certificate; 'issue' signals rearranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: New and clean, like crisp linen.

clue.text: Way to serve potatoes, just stuffed with game

indicators.note: one word filled by another, so the game goes inside the word for just

explanation.surface: Potatoes stuffed with game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed with' suggests a recipe, but it is the container signal. Duchesse potatoes are mash beaten with egg, piped and baked.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are mash with egg piped into swirls and baked, a style of preparation.

clue.text: Unwatered stock

definitions.meaning: a drink served without water
cattle

explanation.surface: Livestock left without water.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky without water is served this way; cattle are an old word for livestock.

clue.text: Christmas present drawer

parts.note: not a drawer holding gifts but an animal that pulls Santa's sleigh of presents

explanation.surface: A drawer where Christmas gifts are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' means one who draws, i.e. pulls, Santa's sleigh of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh of gifts is pulled by a team of antlered animals.

clue.text: Came in to change the pictures

indicators.note: changing the order of these letters gives a new word

explanation.surface: Someone arrived to swap the paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pictures' is British for a film theatre, not paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is British for going to see a film.

clue.text: Hasten the construction of a deep exit

indicators.note: constructing something new out of these letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Speeding up building work on a deep exit.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed something along is to make it happen faster.

clue.text: Even when frayed it should be kept

definitions.text: Even when frayed it should be kept

parts.words: Even when frayed it should be kept
parts.note: one can have frayed nerves of this kind yet should still keep it, not lose it

explanation.surface: Advice about keeping worn fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frayed' suggests cloth; one keeps or loses this, and it can become frayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's composure is something one keeps or loses.
